title: What happens when you click Login? (in the car, front seats)
note: Rewritten 2026-10-09 for natural, realistic speech (same topic and order as dialogue_v1). The human sits in the FRONT passenger seat beside Claude. Voices: local Kokoro TTS (Apache-2.0, commercial use OK), creator's decision; the creator listens and picks voices.

intro.action: the human walks out of the building door and stops at the curb, texting
chat UI: the message is typed in the input bar, sent as a bubble, then Claude replies
intro.phoneReply: On my way! I'll be there in about two minutes.

intro.action: the yellow car pulls up to the curb; the passenger door is on his side

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: Yeah, home. Thanks. Can I ask you something kind of dumb?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.look: quick glance, back to the road
lines.text: Those are my favorite kind. Go for it.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: When I hit log in on a website... what actually happens?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: So, your browser packs up your email and your password, and sends them to the server.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: Wait. It just sends my password? Like, the actual password?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: It does, but over an encrypted connection. And a good server never keeps it. It only stores a scrambled version. A hash.

lines.speaker: human
lines.look: out of the right window, then Claude
lines.text: Okay... so how does it know it's me?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.look: at the road, glance at him at the end
lines.text: It scrambles what you just typed the same way, and compares the two. If they match, you're in.

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Then it hands you a token. Kind of like a wristband at a concert. You show it with every request, so you don't have to log in again each time.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: Huh. So being logged in is basically just... wearing the wristband.

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Exactly. Until it expires. Anyway, we're almost at your place.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: That was weirdly helpful. Thanks, Claude.

cutRule: interior: while CLAUDE speaks use CAM_HUMAN_POV (from the passenger seat: Claude's face and the road), while the HUMAN speaks use CAM_CLAUDE_POV (from the driver side: the human's face, the right window behind him); optional CAM_INT_TwoShot for reactions; cut on the first word, hold at least 1.2 s; the 0.35 s gap stays on the previous shot. No rear-view mirror shots any more.
